title: Transition property lists and discrete transitions overview
learningObjectives: Explain transition property lists and discrete transitions overview and use visual effects responsibly.

understand.concept: The transition shorthand can specify property, duration, timing function, and delay. Multiple transitions are separated by commas. Some properties interpolate continuously, while discrete properties switch between values; newer CSS transition behaviour can allow selected discrete transitions in supported browsers.
understand.whyItMatters: Transitioning all properties can create unintended motion. Name the properties that should animate and check support before relying on discrete transitions or display transitions.
understand.analogy: A transition list is a schedule that tells the browser which changes should be smoothed and how long each should take.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS compositing and animation timelines follow browser rendering rules.

explain.narrative: The background and transform animate over 200 milliseconds. Other property changes are not implicitly included.

examples.explanation: The background and transform animate over 200 milliseconds. Other property changes are not implicitly included.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the visual effect or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create a transition list for two properties. Compare it with transition:all and explain why an explicit list is safer.
practise.independentTask: Build a visual component using the effect. Include a fallback, check contrast, and test keyboard and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Keep essential content independent of visual effects.
Check browser support and fallback behaviour.

questions.prompt: How are multiple transition definitions separated in the shorthand?
questions.explanation: A comma separates each transition entry in the transition shorthand.

questions.prompt: What should accompany an advanced visual effect?
options: A readable fallback and accessible content
Essential meaning available only through the effect
An assumption that all browsers support it
questions.answer: A readable fallback and accessible content
questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement keeps the interface usable when effects are unsupported or disabled.
